subject: Clarify billing for tiny/sliced requests and KV cache interaction
messages:
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@acme.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Billing for very small completions and cache implications

Hi Dylan,

Quick question as we're finalizing the SOW: some of our product flows issue a large number of very short completions (single-token confirmations or 1-2 token replies) — e.g., event pings that map to "ACK" or small metadata labels. How should these be accounted for under Redwood's billing model?

Specifics we care about:
- If a request triggers only a 1-token response, does Redwood round up to any minimum token quantum or charge exactly based on tokenization?
- We also plan to enable prefix caching / KV cache for some routes. If the prefix is cached and only the final token is generated per request, do we get billed for the cached tokens each time or only for the new generated tokens?
- Any practical guidance you can give on minimizing unit-cost for these high-cardinality tiny requests?

We're trying to understand whether to batch client events client-side, add middleware aggregation, or ask for a pricing concession given volume.

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Lee
Head of Platform Integrations, Acme AI

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 11:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Billing for very small completions and cache implications

Thanks Jordan — good, detailed questions. Short answers up front, longer below and I included Marissa (pricing) and Ben (solutions) to flag operational options.

Short answers:
- Rounding: we bill based on tokenized input + output with a per-request minimum of 3 chargeable tokens for streaming endpoints (this is to avoid microbilling noise). For non-streaming requests the minimum is 1 token.
- KV/prefix cache: we DO NOT re-charge the customer for cached KV prefix tokens on reads — billing is for newly generated tokens only. However, there is an internal cache warm-up charge pattern when we first materialize a cache entry (first request that creates the prefix may incur full token cost).
- Minimizing unit cost: batching at the client (grouping several pings into a single request), increasing use of prefix caching, and using a dedicated lightweight model variant (quantized) for these tiny responses are common approaches.

Full details / caveats:
- Minimums and streaming vs non-streaming: the streaming minimum exists because of the per-connection overhead and the continuous batching runtime; for customers with very high QPS of 1-token streaming responses we can discuss an adjusted minimum in the contract.
- Cache semantics: cached KV entries are treated as zero-billed reads; the billing meter looks at the final model input at the tokenization boundary. If a request can be rewritten to rely on a persistent cache key (instead of re-sending the same prompt tokens each time), you'll only pay for the tail generated tokens.
- Round-trip tokenization quirks: sometimes short client payloads tokenize into multiple hidden tokens (e.g., emojis, non-ascii). We'll provide a tokenization sample report (see attached usage-report-2027-04-21.csv) so you can estimate real costs.

Ben / Marissa — can you confirm the contractual path for an exception if Acme's throughput is 10M tiny requests/day and they want a lower per-request minimum? Also flag any pre-approval we need from Finance to offer a temporary pilot concession.

Dylan
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 12:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Billing for very small completions and cache implications

Dylan — a few precision notes to make sure legal/finance get the right language in the SOW: 

1) Minimums: the standard public docs state a per-request minimum of 1 token; the streaming-specific 3-token floor is applied at the runtime layer as an enforcement for hosted streaming endpoints. For Dedicated customers we can map the runtime-flooring to billing differently if they opt for reserved capacity.

2) Cache write/warm-up: clarify that the initial cache materialization expense is charged once per unique prefix per model-version (we record a cache-key creation event). After that, reads are not billed for the cached tokens — but note: if the cache TTL expires and later a request re-warms the cache, that new write will be charged.

3) Aggregation alternatives: If Acme cannot change client behavior, we can offer a middleware aggregator (hosted as a route on Redwood Dedicated) which will collect events for X seconds or Y items and then call the model once. We typically propose X=200ms or Y=25 as defaults for balancing latency vs unit-cost.

4) Contract concession framework: For pilots (30–90 days) we can offer a temporary adjustment to the streaming minimum for this route (e.g., reduce to 1 token floor) in exchange for commitment to a minimum monthly usage or a graduated discount schedule. Finance needs approximate projected tiny-requests/day numbers to fast-track approval.

I'll draft suggested SOW clause language and a short memo for Finance.

—Marissa
Head of Pricing, Redwood Inference

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 09:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Billing for very small completions and cache implications

Jordan — following up with the specifics and a pilot option. Key points summarized for the SOW: 

- Metering: charges are tokenized input + generated tokens. For hosted streaming endpoints we apply a 3-token runtime billing floor; non-streaming endpoints charge at 1 token minimum.
- KV cache: initial cache materialization is charged once per unique prefix per model-version; subsequent reads are not charged. If TTL expires and the prefix is rematerialized, a new charge occurs.
- Pilot concession: Redwood can run a 60-day pilot for the event route that lowers the streaming floor to 1 token for that route only, provided Acme commits to a minimum monthly usage of $12,000 during the pilot. After the pilot we’ll reconcile actual usage and apply either standard pricing or a negotiated discounted rate.

Attached: SOW-draft-v2.pdf (markup highlighting the cache + minimums clause) and the usage-report-2027-04-21.csv sample tokens. Also linking our tokenization FAQ and an example aggregator pattern if you want to avoid a pricing concession.

Next steps: if you can confirm expected tiny-request QPS (or daily count) we’ll route to Finance to get the pilot approved and produce a signed SOW.

Best,
Dylan
